A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SKEL-CF and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and five-page appendices. The complete material supports reliable comparison, including content relocated between the main paper and appendix.

before.justification: v5 reports original SKEL-CF benchmark results, component and refinement ablations, qualitative reconstructions, and attention analyses.

after.justification: v6 retains these empirical results and adds component-ablation results, a camera-translation comparison, and a qualitative analysis of 2D metric limitations.

M1.justification: The backbone, decoder, frozen focal-length predictor, SKEL annotation-fitting procedure, and losses remain unchanged. Section 3.2 clarifies existing decoder conditioning and residual refinement. PnP is evaluated as an alternative, not incorporated into the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage are retained. MOYO-HARD already appears in v5, including its front-camera, middle-50% selection and 9,725 images. The added ablations and camera diagnostic examine existing datasets and outputs rather than introducing new coverage.

E2.justification: v6 Table 5 adds a PnP camera-translation comparator using ground-truth 2D keypoints against the encoder prediction. Existing SKEL, SMPL, and COCO keypoint comparator sets remain unchanged after matching relocated tables.

E3.justification: The new EMDB diagnostic evaluates translation L2 and coordinate-wise errors plus FPS on H100, with ground-truth 2D keypoints supplied to PnP. The ablations add an Only Cam control. Existing training settings, dataset selections, and benchmark metrics are unchanged; the expanded main-text training description was already in v5's appendix.

E4.justification: v6 substantially expands evidence about component contributions: Tables 3 and S3 add an Only Cam control and extend component ablations to 3DPW and MOYO-HARD. Table 5 newly tests encoder camera prediction against PnP, while Figure 5 examines how similar 2D projections conceal different 3D poses. Existing refinement and attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for these experiments. v6 adds results without changing uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Matched existing benchmark, refinement, COCO, and camera-factorization scores are unchanged. v6 adds component-ablation entries and camera diagnostics: encoder versus PnP translation L2 is 0.4223 versus 0.4188, with 91.7 versus 84.7 FPS on H100. These are additional diagnostic results, not improvements over v5's reported benchmark performance.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)-(6) retain the same definitions and objectives. Corrected parameter-set braces and expanded explanations do not change the mathematics. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction drops the claim that even one refinement step yields noticeable gains and replaces the broad state-of-the-art contribution statement with an integrated SKEL recovery contribution. Refinement benefits on challenging MOYO-HARD motions receive greater emphasis. The central method, dataset contribution, and headline MOYO performance claim remain.

C2.justification: v6 explicitly qualifies COCO PCK as a complementary projection metric that can miss 3D errors and discusses mismatched 2D/3D supervision. It distinguishes annotation gains from subsequent pipeline gains and explains why PnP's small accuracy benefit, privileged keypoints, and extra computation favor retaining encoder camera prediction.

D1.justification: v6 specifies H100 hardware for the new timing comparison and redirects supplementary-video access from named folders to the project page. The introduction replaces the future data/code-release promise with an implementation link already present in both abstracts. Architecture, optimizer, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time details otherwise move from the appendix unchanged.

R1.justification: v6 more explicitly positions the contribution as integrating established components for SKEL-specific recovery and foregrounds DETR inspiration in the introduction. This refines contribution positioning without expanding the cited research set: the additional bibliography entry duplicates the already cited SKEL paper.

P1.justification: The introduction, contribution bullets, refinement explanation, and ablation discussion receive localized rewrites. Implementation details move into Section 3.2, the appendix is reorganized, and acknowledgments are added. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: Table 2 becomes a compact main-text table plus complete Table S2; the COCO comparison moves to Table S1; component ablations become Tables 3 and S3; and a camera table and PCK figure are added. Figures 3 and 4 absorb examples previously in Figures S4 and S3. These are deliberate display changes beyond pagination or renumbering.

improvement.justification: The added Only Cam control, broader component ablations, and PnP diagnostic provide better support for specific design choices. The explicit limitations of COCO PCK also improve interpretation. These are useful but bounded gains: the method and headline results remain unchanged, and comparisons moved out of the main text remain available in the appendix.
